title: Maiale con Lenticchie
subtitle: Italian pork with lentils
excerpt: Maiale con lenticchie is one of the great cucina povera combinations of central Italy: a pork joint slow-braised with lentils, soffritto, red wine, and rosemary. The lentils absorb the pork juices as they cook and turn into a thick, smoky, savoury base. The dish is eaten at New Year across Italy as a symbol of prosperity.
sourceNotes: Pork with lentils is one of the most traditional Italian winter dishes, strongly associated with New Year feasts. In Umbria and Lazio, cotechino (a poaching sausage) with lentils is the canonical New Year dish, but braised pork with lentils is the everyday version. The lentils symbolise coins and therefore prosperity in the new year.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well. Reheat gently with a splash of water.

content.text: Use small brown or green lentils that hold their shape during cooking. Puy lentils work well; red lentils will turn to mush. The pork shoulder braises in the same pot as the lentils, so the lentils absorb all the meat juices. No soaking is needed for small lentils.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a large heavy pan over medium-high heat. Season {{pork-shoulder}} pork with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Brown on all sides, about 6 minutes total. Remove and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add {{onion}} onion, {{celery}} celery, and {{carrot}} carrot to the pan and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{rosemary}} rosemary and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{red-wine}} wine and simmer for 3 minutes until reduced by half.

Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and {{lentils-green}} lentils. Return the pork to the pan. Add enough water to just cover the lentils (about 600 ml). Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 60 to 70 minutes until the lentils are completely tender and the pork is soft enough to break apart with a spoon. Check every 20 minutes and add water if the lentils look dry. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Remove the rosemary sprigs before serving.

items.symptom: The lentils are still firm after 60 minutes
items.cause: Old lentils take longer to cook. Adding salt too early can also slow them.
items.fix: Add {{salt-table}} salt only in the last 15 minutes of cooking. Continue simmering, checking every 10 minutes and adding water as needed.

content.text: Pork with lentils is the New Year dish of Italy. In Umbria and Lazio, cotechino sausage with lentils is the canonical version, but braised pork shoulder with lentils is made year-round. The lentil is associated with coins and good fortune in Italian tradition -- the small round shape is said to resemble money. The dish is a fixture of cucina povera cooking across Umbria, Lazio, and Emilia-Romagna.
